note: Different facility/camera from the delivery_*/teevra.mov and clip_144626/144954/145619.mp4 sessions -- this one has a full set of yellow/green plastic training stumps-on-a-base at BOTH ends of the netted lane (fixed fisheye-style tripod near the batting end looking down the pitch at a bowler bowling toward these same near stumps). near_stump_height_px measured from frame 2000 (off/leg stump, x~865-878): top edge y~685, top-of-base-plate y~982 (297px), same technique as delivery_4_calib.json -- excludes the plastic base's decorative collar bulge (~y960-980) and flat plate (~y982-1002), which is NOT part of the regulation 0.711m stump height. far_stump_height_px measured from frame 6900 (least-occluded frame found; the far-end batsman stands right next to his own stumps most of the time, see runs/frontViewVideo candidate scan) -- far stumps are only ~50px tall total (top y~490, ground y~540) and too small to reliably separate stump from base directly, so (per delivery_4_calib.json's same method) this applies the near set's measured stump-only/total-height ratio (297/317 = 0.937) to the far set's total height (50px): 50 * 0.937 = 46.9px. Camera confirmed fixed (tripod) across multiple widely-separated frames (0, 500, 2000, 6900+) -- stump pixel positions at both ends are stable throughout. This video's runs/frontViewVideo/detections.json predates pipeline/zoom_track_detect.py (no candidates_zoom_track.json exists for it) -- it was last generated by an older pipeline version and has no speed_method field; re-running pipeline/run.py on it (21127 frames, no ROI file yet) will pick up this calibration but has not been done as part of adding this file. On-frame reference points for the viewer overlay (near_points/far_points, each [top,bottom]) were added after the fact for visualization only -- top points were located by direct pixel inspection of measured_frame; bottom points are top_y + the already-recorded near/far_stump_height_px above (not independently re-measured), so the drawn segment length always matches the numeric calibration value even where the true base is partly occluded (e.g. by the far-end batsman standing at his own stumps).
